statement: Let n = len(arr) and let d = min_{0 <= i < j < n} |arr[i] - arr[j]|. The function returns a result r such that r is exactly the list, in strictly ascending lexicographic order, of all pairs [a,b] for which: (1) a <= b; (2) a occurs in arr and b occurs in arr; (3) b - a = d; and (4) if a = b then a occurs at least twice in arr, i.e. there exist i < j with arr[i] = arr[j] = a. 'Exactly' means that for every such [a,b] there is exactly one index k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k] = [a,b], and every index k with 0 <= k < len(r) has len(r[k]) = 2 and r[k] equal to one of those pairs. 'Strictly ascending lexicographic order' means for every k with 0 <= k < len(r)-1, either r[k][0] < r[k+1][0], or r[k][0] = r[k+1][0] and r[k][1] < r[k+1][1].
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2 and len(arr) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail.

Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair of integers [a,b] such that a <= b, both a and b occur in arr, b - a = d, and (if a = b then a occurs at least twice in arr), there exists k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k] = [a,b].
